hw-u4-q07.hint: Your label should reflect what the evidence actually establishes.
hw-u4-q07.explanation: Recording uncertainty preserves the hypothesis without presenting it as a confirmed connection.
solutionSteps: Recording uncertainty preserves the hypothesis without presenting it as a confirmed connection.
Choose B: “Possible UART TX; verification needed”.

hw-u4-q08.title: Compare documents with the actual board
hw-u4-q08.statement: An online schematic places flash memory beside the processor, but your board has a different component there. What is the best response?

options.a: Check whether the schematic matches your model and revision
options.b: Assume the visible component must be flash
options.c: Replace your observation with the schematic’s description

hw-u4-q08.hint: A document’s relevance depends on which hardware it describes.
hw-u4-q08.explanation: Resolve the mismatch before using that document as evidence for your board.
solutionSteps: Resolve the mismatch before using that document as evidence for your board.
Choose A: Check whether the schematic matches your model and revision.

hw-u4-q09.title: An update file may be a container
hw-u4-q09.statement: You obtain an official update file for the correct device. Can you assume it is a byte-for-byte image of the entire flash chip?

options.a: Yes, because all official updates use that format
options.b: Yes, if the filename contains “firmware”
options.c: No; first establish the package’s format and contents

hw-u4-q09.hint: A file used to perform an update can contain more than the installed program.
hw-u4-q09.explanation: Correct model compatibility does not establish the file’s internal layout or its relationship to physical storage.
solutionSteps: Correct model compatibility does not establish the file’s internal layout or its relationship to physical storage.
Choose C: No; first establish the package’s format and contents.

hw-u4-q10.title: Preserve the original and check copies
hw-u4-q10.statement: Your original and working copy have matching SHA-256 hashes. What does this support?

options.a: The firmware has no vulnerabilities
options.b: The files have the same contents
options.c: The manufacturer has authenticated the download

hw-u4-q10.hint: Comparing hashes checks content equality, not trustworthiness.
hw-u4-q10.explanation: The comparison supports an unchanged copy. Authenticity requires a trusted verification method or reference.
solutionSteps: The comparison supports an unchanged copy. Authenticity requires a trusted verification method or reference.
Choose B: The files have the same contents.

hw-u4-q11.title: Interpret strings and entropy as clues
hw-u4-q11.statement: A firmware section has high entropy. Which next step is best supported?

options.a: Check headers and format evidence to distinguish possible explanations
options.b: Declare the section encrypted
options.c: Declare the section empty

hw-u4-q11.hint: More than one process can produce highly varied bytes.
hw-u4-q11.explanation: Examine additional evidence before choosing between compression, encryption or another explanation.
solutionSteps: Examine additional evidence before choosing between compression, encryption or another explanation.
Choose A: Check headers and format evidence to distinguish possible explanations.

hw-u4-q12.title: Combine evidence without overstating access
hw-u4-q12.statement: A processor supports UART, nearby pads are labelled TX/RX, and a firmware file contains “console.” No signal has been captured. Which conclusion is strongest?

options.a: An unrestricted command console is confirmed
options.b: The pads are confirmed to be inactive
options.c: The pads are plausible UART candidates, but their activity and access remain unverified

hw-u4-q12.hint: Separate a promising hypothesis from a demonstrated capability.
hw-u4-q12.explanation: The clues justify further identification and measurement. They do not yet establish an active interface, a console or unrestricted access.
solutionSteps: The clues justify further identification and measurement. They do not yet establish an active interface, a console or unrestricted access.
Choose C: The pads are plausible UART candidates, but their activity and access remain unverified.

hw-u1-q16.title: Understanding attack effort
hw-u1-q16.statement: A defence makes an attack much more expensive but does not prevent it completely. What has it achieved?

options.a: It has made every attack impossible.
options.b: It has increased the effort required for that attack.
options.c: It has reduced the value of the protected information.

hw-u1-q16.hint: Separate the cost of obtaining an asset from the asset’s value.
hw-u1-q16.explanation: The defence raises the attack’s cost. That can discourage an attacker, but the path may still be possible.
solutionSteps: The defence raises the attack’s cost. That can discourage an attacker, but the path may still be possible.
Choose B: It has increased the effort required for that attack.

hw-u1-q17.title: Knowing which verification key to trust
hw-u1-q17.statement: An update includes a verification key. Before trusting signatures checked with it, what must the device establish?

options.a: That the key is authorised by an existing trusted reference.
options.b: That the key is stored in the same file as the update.
options.c: That the signature and key have matching filenames.

hw-u1-q17.hint: Consider whether an attacker could supply both the software and a new key.
hw-u1-q17.explanation: A matching signature alone does not establish authorisation if the verification key is untrusted.
solutionSteps: A matching signature alone does not establish authorisation if the verification key is untrusted.
Choose A: That the key is authorised by an existing trusted reference.

hw-u1-q18.title: Continuing the checks during startup
hw-u1-q18.statement: Boot ROM verifies a bootloader, but that bootloader runs an unchecked application. Where is the missing verification?

options.a: Between power-on and the boot ROM.
options.b: In the already completed bootloader check.
options.c: Between the bootloader and the application.

hw-u1-q18.hint: Follow the stages in execution order.
hw-u1-q18.explanation: Verifying the bootloader does not automatically verify everything it loads.
solutionSteps: Verifying the bootloader does not automatically verify everything it loads.
Choose C: Between the bootloader and the application.

hw-u1-q19.title: Using a secret without revealing it
hw-u1-q19.statement: Which information should the normal application receive in this arrangement?

options.a: The secret signing key.
options.b: The resulting signature.
options.c: A copy of the protected environment’s memory.

hw-u1-q19.hint: Distinguish the result of an operation from the secret used to perform it.
hw-u1-q19.explanation: The application needs the signature. Keeping the key isolated reduces its exposure, provided the isolation works correctly.
solutionSteps: The application needs the signature. Keeping the key isolated reduces its exposure, provided the isolation works correctly.
Choose B: The resulting signature.

hw-u1-q20.title: Reporting a weakness clearly
hw-u1-q20.statement: Which report gives the vendor the clearest starting point?

options.a: “Your products probably have security problems.”
options.b: “This device looks similar to another vulnerable product.”
options.c: “Model X, firmware Y exposes private records when these steps are followed.”

hw-u1-q20.hint: Look for information that lets someone repeat the observation.
hw-u1-q20.explanation: It identifies the affected configuration and provides a reproducible finding.
solutionSteps: It identifies the affected configuration and provides a reproducible finding.
Choose C: “Model X, firmware Y exposes private records when these steps are followed.”

hw-u2-q16.title: What a capacitor does
hw-u2-q16.statement: Where does the energy powering the indicator after disconnection come from?

options.a: Energy previously stored in the capacitor.
options.b: Energy continuously created by the capacitor.
options.c: Energy produced by the disconnected supply cable.

hw-u2-q16.hint: Consider what happened while the supply was still connected.
hw-u2-q16.explanation: The capacitor releases previously stored energy; it does not generate a continuing supply.
solutionSteps: The capacitor releases previously stored energy; it does not generate a continuing supply.
Choose A: Energy previously stored in the capacitor.

hw-u2-q17.title: Charging through a resistor
hw-u2-q17.statement: An uncharged capacitor connects to a 5 V supply through a resistor. What should happen to its voltage?

options.a: It stays at zero while connected.
options.b: It immediately becomes 5 V, regardless of the resistor.
options.c: It rises towards 5 V over time.

hw-u2-q17.hint: Apply what you know about a resistor limiting current.
hw-u2-q17.explanation: Limited charging current means the capacitor’s voltage takes time to rise.
solutionSteps: Limited charging current means the capacitor’s voltage takes time to rise.
Choose C: It rises towards 5 V over time.

hw-u2-q18.title: Helping a chip through a brief current demand
hw-u2-q18.statement: Why place a decoupling capacitor near a processor’s supply connection?

options.a: To store the processor’s instructions.
options.b: To help stabilise its local supply during rapid current changes.
options.c: To select the processor’s communication address.

hw-u2-q18.hint: Focus on what changes when the processor suddenly needs more current.
hw-u2-q18.explanation: The capacitor provides local support for short changes in demand.
solutionSteps: The capacitor provides local support for short changes in demand.
Choose B: To help stabilise its local supply during rapid current changes.

hw-u2-q19.title: Understanding the limit of that support
hw-u2-q19.statement: Why can the same capacitor handle a short interruption but fail during a much longer one?

options.a: The circuit eventually uses too much of its stored energy.
options.b: The capacitor becomes a resistor after a fixed time.
options.c: The capacitor stores energy only while the circuit is off.

hw-u2-q19.hint: Compare the energy available with the energy consumed over time.
hw-u2-q19.explanation: A longer interruption requires more energy than the capacitor may be able to provide.
solutionSteps: A longer interruption requires more energy than the capacitor may be able to provide.
Choose A: The circuit eventually uses too much of its stored energy.

hw-u2-q20.title: What an inductor does
hw-u2-q20.statement: Which statement correctly compares capacitors and inductors?

options.a: Both primarily oppose changes in voltage.
options.b: Capacitors oppose changes in current; inductors oppose changes in voltage.
options.c: Capacitors oppose rapid voltage changes; inductors oppose rapid current changes.

hw-u2-q20.hint: Recall which electrical quantity changed as the capacitor charged.
hw-u2-q20.explanation: Capacitor behaviour relates to changing voltage; inductor behaviour relates to changing current.
solutionSteps: Capacitor behaviour relates to changing voltage; inductor behaviour relates to changing current.
Choose C: Capacitors oppose rapid voltage changes; inductors oppose rapid current changes.

hw-u2-q21.title: A diode’s direction matters
hw-u2-q21.statement: Why can reversing a diode change whether current flows through a circuit?

options.a: Reversing it changes the resistor’s resistance.
options.b: The diode’s conduction depends on its orientation relative to the applied voltage.
options.c: Reversing it increases the battery’s stored energy.

hw-u2-q21.hint: Consider which component’s direction-dependent behaviour has changed.
hw-u2-q21.explanation: A diode behaves differently under forward and reverse voltage, within its operating limits.
solutionSteps: A diode behaves differently under forward and reverse voltage, within its operating limits.
Choose B: The diode’s conduction depends on its orientation relative to the applied voltage.

hw-u2-q22.title: Controlling a separate current path
hw-u2-q22.statement: In this arrangement, which component switches the indicator’s supply-current path?

options.a: The transistor.
options.b: The processor’s program memory.
options.c: The decoupling capacitor.

hw-u2-q22.hint: Separate the component issuing the command from the component switching the load.
hw-u2-q22.explanation: The processor provides control; the transistor switches the load’s current path.
solutionSteps: The processor provides control; the transistor switches the load’s current path.
Choose A: The transistor.

hw-u2-q23.title: Producing the required supply voltage
hw-u2-q23.statement: Which component is responsible for converting the board’s 9 V input into its regulated 3.3 V supply?

options.a: The processor’s switching transistor.
options.b: The decoupling capacitor alone.
options.c: The voltage regulator.

hw-u2-q23.hint: Identify the component designed to maintain the output supply level.
hw-u2-q23.explanation: The regulator produces the required rail; capacitors help manage changes around it.
solutionSteps: The regulator produces the required rail; capacitors help manage changes around it.
Choose C: The voltage regulator.

hw-u2-q24.title: Recognising variation on a DC supply
hw-u2-q24.statement: A processor’s 3.3 V rail briefly falls to 3.0 V without reversing polarity. How should you describe it?

options.a: A perfectly constant DC voltage.
options.b: A DC supply containing a voltage disturbance.
options.c: A voltage that necessarily alternates between positive and negative.

hw-u2-q24.hint: Separate changing magnitude from changing polarity.
hw-u2-q24.explanation: The voltage varies, but it retains its polarity.
solutionSteps: The voltage varies, but it retains its polarity.
Choose B: A DC supply containing a voltage disturbance.

hw-u2-q25.title: Letting devices take turns
hw-u2-q25.statement: A stops transmitting and B begins. What should A’s output do while B drives the shared wire?

options.a: Drive the opposite voltage to B.
options.b: Continue driving its last value.
options.c: Enter high impedance.

hw-u2-q25.hint: Consider how A can avoid competing with B’s output.
hw-u2-q25.explanation: High impedance lets B control the wire without A actively driving against it.
solutionSteps: High impedance lets B control the wire without A actively driving against it.
Choose C: Enter high impedance.

hw-u2-q26.title: Preserving fast signal details
hw-u2-q26.statement: The probe is smoothing a signal’s fast edges. Which change addresses that limitation most directly?

options.a: Use a suitable probe with adequate bandwidth.
options.b: Record more samples through the same unsuitable probe.
options.c: Display the same capture over a longer time window.

hw-u2-q26.hint: Identify where the waveform loses detail.
hw-u2-q26.explanation: The measurement path must preserve the fast features before sampling can represent them.
solutionSteps: The measurement path must preserve the fast features before sampling can represent them.
Choose A: Use a suitable probe with adequate bandwidth.

hw-u2-q27.title: Capturing a supply disturbance
hw-u2-q27.statement: A board resets when its supply briefly falls below 2.9 V. Which trigger best targets the falling supply event?

options.a: A rising crossing of 2.9 V on the supply.
options.b: A falling crossing of 2.9 V on the supply.
options.c: A rising transition on an unrelated communication line.

hw-u2-q27.hint: Match both the signal being investigated and its direction of change.
hw-u2-q27.explanation: This setting targets the supply as it falls through the relevant threshold.
solutionSteps: This setting targets the supply as it falls through the relevant threshold.
Choose B: A falling crossing of 2.9 V on the supply.

hw-u3-q19.title: Matching the complete UART format
hw-u3-q19.statement: Your adapter already uses the correct baud rate, but it uses even parity. The device requires 8N1. What should you change?

options.a: Disable parity.
options.b: Reduce the number of data bits to seven.
options.c: Increase the number of stop bits to two.

hw-u3-q19.hint: Check which part of “8N1” describes parity.
hw-u3-q19.explanation: The “N” specifies no parity; the other stated settings need not change.
solutionSteps: The “N” specifies no parity; the other stated settings need not change.
Choose A: Disable parity.

hw-u3-q20.title: Checking electrical compatibility separately
hw-u3-q20.statement: The baud rate and frame format match, but the electrical levels do not. What is needed?

options.a: A different number of stop bits.
options.b: A different terminal character encoding.
options.c: A suitable electrical interface or converter.

hw-u3-q20.hint: Identify whether the mismatch concerns the message format or the voltages carrying it.
hw-u3-q20.explanation: Matching software settings cannot correct incompatible electrical signalling.
solutionSteps: Matching software settings cannot correct incompatible electrical signalling.
Choose C: A suitable electrical interface or converter.

hw-u3-q21.title: Following SPI responses
hw-u3-q21.statement: You captured the controller’s command but now want the sensor’s returned measurement. Which data signal should you inspect?

options.a: COPI.
options.b: CIPO.
options.c: Chip select.

hw-u3-q21.hint: Follow the direction from the sensor back to the controller.
hw-u3-q21.explanation: CIPO carries the peripheral’s outgoing data towards the controller.
solutionSteps: CIPO carries the peripheral’s outgoing data towards the controller.
Choose B: CIPO.

hw-u3-q22.title: Selecting an I²C register before reading
hw-u3-q22.statement: A controller writes 0x10 before reading a sensor’s temperature register. In this arrangement, why does it send 0x10?

options.a: To select the register whose contents it wants.
options.b: To replace the temperature measurement with 0x10.
options.c: To change the sensor’s I²C device address to 0x10.

hw-u3-q22.hint: Distinguish selecting a location from changing the value stored there.
hw-u3-q22.explanation: The initial write selects the register; the subsequent read receives its contents.
solutionSteps: The initial write selects the register; the subsequent read receives its contents.
Choose A: To select the register whose contents it wants.

hw-u3-q23.title: Observing pins without taking control
hw-u3-q23.statement: You want to control selected output pins for a connection test rather than just observe them. Which operation matches that purpose?

options.a: SAMPLE only.
options.b: Either operation, because both provide identical control.
options.c: EXTEST, with attention to its effect on normal operation.

hw-u3-q23.hint: Decide whether the task requires observing or driving the connections.
hw-u3-q23.explanation: EXTEST can control external connections; SAMPLE serves the different purpose of observation.
solutionSteps: EXTEST can control external connections; SAMPLE serves the different purpose of observation.
Choose C: EXTEST, with attention to its effect on normal operation.

hw-u3-q24.title: Recovering timing from the signal
hw-u3-q24.statement: An unfamiliar connection has no separate clock wire. Which conclusion is justified?

options.a: It must be UART.
options.b: Its protocol still needs identifying because several interfaces work without a separate clock wire.
options.c: It cannot communicate using synchronised timing.

hw-u3-q24.hint: An absent clock wire does not mean that the signal contains no timing information.
hw-u3-q24.explanation: The observation narrows some possibilities but does not identify the protocol by itself.
solutionSteps: The observation narrows some possibilities but does not identify the protocol by itself.
Choose B: Its protocol still needs identifying because several interfaces work without a separate clock wire.

hw-u4-q13.title: Choosing a useful documentation source
hw-u4-q13.statement: You have an FCC identifier and want publicly available photographs of the product’s internal board. Which source should you check first?

options.a: The corresponding FCC filing.
options.b: A generic processor programming manual.
options.c: A resistor manufacturer’s package catalogue.

hw-u4-q13.hint: Match the identifier to the organisation and record it identifies.
hw-u4-q13.explanation: The filing may contain product-specific internal photographs, although availability varies.
solutionSteps: The filing may contain product-specific internal photographs, although availability varies.
Choose A: The corresponding FCC filing.

hw-u4-q14.title: Understanding physical access to chip connections
hw-u4-q14.statement: Two chips have the same function, but one has exposed leads and the other has hidden underside connections. Which is generally easier to contact with a suitable lead clip?

options.a: The chip with hidden underside connections.
options.b: Both are equally accessible because their function matches.
options.c: The chip with exposed leads.

hw-u4-q14.hint: Consider what the clip must physically touch.
hw-u4-q14.explanation: Accessible leads provide contact points; matching function does not make the packages equally accessible.
solutionSteps: Accessible leads provide contact points; matching function does not make the packages equally accessible.
Choose C: The chip with exposed leads.

hw-u4-q15.title: Recognising a configurable connection
hw-u4-q15.statement: Why might a manufacturer use a zero-ohm component in this position?

options.a: To provide a precise current-limiting resistance.
options.b: To make the connection optional during assembly.
options.c: To store charge beside the configuration pin.

hw-u4-q15.hint: Think about what changes when the component is fitted or omitted.
hw-u4-q15.explanation: The part provides an assembly-time connection option.
solutionSteps: The part provides an assembly-time connection option.
Choose B: To make the connection optional during assembly.

hw-u4-q16.title: Following a trace between layers
hw-u4-q16.statement: You follow a surface trace until it reaches a via. What should you record?

options.a: The connection may continue on another layer.
options.b: The electrical connection necessarily ends there.
options.c: The via connects the trace to every other signal on the board.

hw-u4-q16.hint: Consider the purpose of having multiple conductive layers.
hw-u4-q16.explanation: A via can transfer the connection between layers; its destination still needs investigation.
solutionSteps: A via can transfer the connection between layers; its destination still needs investigation.
Choose A: The connection may continue on another layer.

hw-u4-q17.title: Checking for available firmware first
hw-u4-q17.statement: You need firmware for initial analysis and have not checked whether a matching update exists. What is the most sensible first step?

options.a: Remove the flash chip immediately.
options.b: Begin capturing every communication interface.
options.c: Check the vendor’s update downloads for the correct device.

hw-u4-q17.hint: Which option could provide the information with the least physical work?
hw-u4-q17.explanation: A matching download may satisfy the task without modifying the hardware.
solutionSteps: A matching download may satisfy the task without modifying the hardware.
Choose C: Check the vendor’s update downloads for the correct device.

hw-u4-q18.title: Interpreting a detected file format
hw-u4-q18.statement: A tool reports a possible compressed section at a particular offset. What is the best next step?

options.a: Assume the entire firmware file is compressed in that format.
options.b: Examine the reported region to check the format and its boundaries.
options.c: Treat the detection as proof that the firmware is encrypted.

hw-u4-q18.hint: Keep the conclusion limited to the region and evidence reported.
hw-u4-q18.explanation: The detection provides a starting point that should be checked before drawing broader conclusions.
solutionSteps: The detection provides a starting point that should be checked before drawing broader conclusions.
Choose B: Examine the reported region to check the format and its boundaries.
